newsitem.title: USA: Clinton warns Japan against "exploding" trade gap.
newsitem.headline: Clinton warns Japan against "exploding" trade gap.

text.p: President Clinton warned Japan on Sunday that a return to "exploding" trade surpluses with the United States would hurt both countries.

"If we return to a time when we've got exploding trade deficits then that will once again move front and center into our relationship in a way that won't be good for either country," Clinton told a news conference.

Speaking after the close of the Group of Seven summit here, Clinton voiced concern that Japan's plans to slash its budget deficit could sap economic demand at home and force it to once again rely on exports to spur growth.

"The decision by the Japanese government to try to pursue a path of fiscal austerity, driven in part by the desire to prepare for the aging of the Japanese population, runs the risk of going back to the old export-driven stratgey of growth," the president said.
"We'll just have to work through those conflicts," Clinton added, "We can't tell the Japanese government or the Japanese people that they can't prepare for the aging of their population."
But neither does the United Staes want to see a return to the exploding trade deficits with Japan of the past.
